title: Distributed Deadlock via Un-Ordered Lock Acquisition
pattern: Acquiring multiple independent locks on separate remote database nodes or consensus services sequentially in an arbitrary, non-deterministic order across concurrent client operations.
why_bad: In a distributed system, network latency and partial failures make lock-acquisition timings unpredictable [20]. If Client 1 acquires `Lock 1` and Client 2 simultaneously acquires `Lock 2`, both will block indefinitely attempting to acquire the remaining lock, creating a classic distributed deadlock [16]. Unlike single-node databases, distributed lock coordinators rarely have a global dependency graph to detect and abort deadlock cycles, leading to permanent resource exhaustion [65, 76].
detection: Identify functions that instantiate or await multiple remote lock acquisition calls (e.g., `acquire_lock`, `lock_resource`) sequentially, where the lock identifiers are not sorted or ordered systematically prior to acquisition.
fix: Sort all target resource identifiers lexicographically or numerically before initiating remote lock requests, ensuring every thread acquires locks in the exact same global order [65]. Alternatively, utilize a Coarse-Grained Lock on a single root coordinator [74].
